newsitem.title: USA: Taiwan not seen cutting off price data for futures.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan not seen cutting off price data for futures.

text.p: Taiwan regulators are unlikely to cut off price data to futures exchanges following a six-month review of trading on Taiwan stock index futures and options in Chicago and Singapore, a Taiwan futures source said.
"I don't think it's likely," Eugene Chang, of the trading firm Taiwan International Futures Corp, said at a news conference hosted by the Chicago Mercantile Exchange.
The CME will launch futures and options on the Dow Jones Taiwan stock index at 1900 CST Wednesday (0100 GMT Thursday) on GLOBEX, the after-hours electronic trading system.

Taiwan regulators have threatened to cut off the flow of stock price data, but Chang said Taiwan's Securities and Exchange Commission would not risk its goal of establishing a more international financial market.
"I don't think the SEC will take this risk," Chang said. "It's a back step to stop the live data feed."

Dow Jones & Co Inc licensed its index, one of some 29 country indexes, to the CME. A unit of Morgan Stanley Group Inc licensed its own Taiwan stock index to the Singapore International Monetary Exchange (SIMEX). Trading in the SIMEX contracts is set to open five minutes before the CME launch.

The CME will offer the product exclusively on GLOBEX, and regular trading hours will be from 1430 to 1030 CST (2030 to 1630 GMT) Monday through Thursday. Trade will start at 1730 CST (2330 GMT) on Sunday.
On Friday evenings, the product will trade from 1830 to 2100 CST (0030 to 0300 GMT) to correspond with cash activity on Saturdays at the Taiwan Stock Exchange.

Taiwanese regulators said on Saturday they did not rule out the possibility of cutting the supply of data to the CME or SIMEX after a six-month review. They have since urged Taiwanese investors not to try trading either contract through "illegal futures brokerages."

"I think it does not prohibit Taiwanese institutions who want to trade from trading in offshore accounts," Rick Kilcollin, CME president-designate, told the news conference. ((Derivatives desk 312-408-8750;E-mail derivatives@reuters.com))
